summary: Odd 5xx pattern linked to healthcheck throttle and upstream crashes
description:
Issue summary: Customer (NimbleDocs) reports a high, recurring 5xx error floor on their streaming endpoints beginning ~2026-03-10 09:10 UTC. Impact: intermittent failures for long-lived streaming sessions (chat + streaming embeddings), elevated tail 5xx rate (~3-5% of requests) and increased latency for successful requests. Environment: production cluster in us-east servicing Dedicated pool for NimbleDocs (pinned model: redwood-ggml-7B).

Observed behavior:
- Error responses are primarily 502/503 with some 500s.
- Errors cluster during tenant warm-up windows and after autoscaler HPA bursts.
- Runtime logs show upstream process exits (exit code 137) and rapid reconnects.
- API gateway reports short-lived healthcheck failures and then applies priority-shed to streaming connections, amplifying 5xx rates.

Expected behavior:
- Streaming sessions should maintain <0.1% 5xx; healthchecks should not cause sustained priority sheds.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start multiple long-lived streaming chat sessions (20 concurrent, ~1MB prompts) to the customer's endpoint.
2) Trigger a model variant update on a subset of the dedicated pool to force a partial warmup.
3) Observe the accept-queue and healthcheck metrics on the tenant pool.

Logs / Evidence attached inline in comments: excerpts of runtime stderr, apigw accept-queue metrics, autoscaler events, and NVML reset timestamps.

Customer impact note: NimbleDocs saw partial degradation affecting a subset of production user sessions (estimated 12% of active streaming sessions experienced at least one 5xx in the 30m window). They are on a Dedicated plan; work needs prioritization.
investigation_notes: 10:05 UTC - Initial triage (Ariana): Alarm from customer-facing monitor and slack channel #support-alerts. Spike in 5xx rate coincides with autoscaler HPA scaling event for the dedicated pool.
10:30 UTC - Observed apigw metrics: accept_queue_depth increased from baseline 2 -> 48 for tenant. Tail latencies rose concurrently. Healthcheck failure count spiked for 3 worker pods.

10:42 UTC - Runtime logs: three downstream worker processes terminated with exit code 137 within a 90s window. Kernel OOM not present; NVML logs show GPU driver reset on one host around same timestamp.

11:15 UTC - Hypothesis A: Autoscaler-induced prewarm/warmup caused temporary CPU/gpu contention on a subset of nodes; healthchecks started failing and apigw started marking nodes as unhealthy, triggering priority-shed, which amplified retry/reconnect pressure and increased 5xx floor.

11:45 UTC - Hypothesis B: A connection leak in the runtime proxy kept accept queues artificially high, delaying healthcheck responses which the apigw interprets as unhealthy; combined with HPA churning this produced cascading evictions.
12:05 UTC - Evidence against pure memory OOM: dmesg and node-exporter memory graphs show <70% memory usage; but NVML shows a GPU reset (driver) that correlates with process exits on that host.
12:30 UTC - Quick correlation: streaming sessions with large initial prompts (>0.8MB) more likely to see 5xx; suggests an accept-queue processing time sensitivity to payload size during warmup.
13:00 UTC - Cross-ref: linked SUP-314271 shows similar accept-queue growth during warmup but for a different customer; pattern consistent with accept-queue backpressure + healthcheck timeouts.

13:30 UTC - Action taken: temporarily increased healthcheck timeout for affected dedicated pool and disabled aggressive priority-shed for streaming routes to allow in-flight reconnections while we stabilize nodes. Began controlled draining of the two suspect nodes for deeper analysis.
14:10 UTC - Result: immediate reduction in 5xx rate from ~4.6% -> ~0.9% over 20 minutes for NimbleDocs traffic. No customer-visible rollout yet; monitoring continues.

Todo: Collect full NVML stacks for the suspect hosts, run stress test reproducer with long streaming sessions and large prompts in staging with HPA churn enabled, and review runtime proxy connection handling for leak patterns.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Nina Park (Support): Acknowledged ticket with customer. Asked for sample request IDs and timestamps. Customer provided sample request IDs: req_20260310_0912_azf3, req_20260310_0918_4v9k.
2026-03-10 11:00 - Ravi Kapoor (SRE): Investigating node-level metrics. Spotted GPU driver reset on host redwood-us-east-2b-45 at 09:11:08 UTC. Pinpointing corresponding runtime process IDs.

2026-03-10 12:20 - Ariana Cole (Support): Applied temporary healthcheck timeout increase and relaxed priority-shed on the customer's streaming route per SRE recommendation. Customer observing fewer failures — monitoring closely.
2026-03-10 13:05 - Ravi Kapoor (SRE): Drained pod runtime-nd-215 on host redwood-us-east-2b-45 for forensic dump. Collected core dumps and NVML logs; shipping to infra-research team (see PR link).

2026-03-10 13:40 - Infra Research (comment): NVML trace indicates a GPU firmware transient that triggered a minor driver reset; runtime's crash-recovery loop then failed to respect backoff which led to aggressive reconnects. Filing internal PR to add jitter and exponential backoff to crash-restart path. (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6421)

2026-03-11 09:18 - Customer (NimbleDocs Support Lead Sarah Jensen): Confirmed degradation window matches their customer reports. Thank you for quick interim fix; requesting postmortem and permanent mitigation timeline.

2026-03-12 10:50 - Ravi Kapoor (SRE): Implemented staged fix in canary: added 2s randomized backoff to runtime restart loop and increased healthcheck grace window for warmup periods. Observations: canary shows stable healthchecks during synthetic HPA churn. Scheduling wider rollout pending validation.
resolution: Workaround applied: increased healthcheck timeout and relaxed priority-shed for NimbleDocs dedicated pool; drained and quarantined two suspect nodes. Long-term fix in progress: add randomized exponential backoff to runtime crash-restart loop and improve detection of GPU driver reset to avoid immediate restarts; also add accept-queue backpressure smoothing during autoscaler events. Planned rollout: staged canary 2026-03-12, broader rollout if 24h canary stability OK. Customer to receive postmortem and follow-up on 2026-03-13.
